key_insight: How training data is ordered can meaningfully change LLM training efficiency and outcomes, even when the data itself stays the same. The paper shows that smart data organization is a simple but underexplored lever for improving training in the one-to-few-epoch regime.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of understanding about how to organize training data for large language models, beyond just selecting which data to use. The challenge is that most LLM training runs only a small number of epochs, making the sequence and grouping of samples potentially important for learning efficiency.
method: Reuses pre-computed sample-level scores to study different data ordering strategies without retraining score models from scratch.
Systematically compares how alternative organization schemes affect training behavior and model performance.
Focuses on practical training regimes where data is seen only once or a few times, making ordering effects more pronounced.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that better training pipelines may be achieved not only through data filtering, but also through smarter data arrangement. This can improve efficiency and performance with minimal additional cost.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing data selection vs. data organization
A comparison chart of different ordering strategies and their training outcomes
An epoch timeline illustrating one-pass or few-pass training
An icon-based flow showing sample-level scores being reused to guide ordering
paper_title: Demystifying Data Organization for Enhanced LLM Training
paper_authors: Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Tongshen Yang, Yonghan Wang, Xin Zhang
